messages:
Tony (Customer): Getting a 413 from /v1/rerank, response body just 'Payload too large'. Sending ~150 docs, total ~1.2MB. Anyone seen this?
Maya (Support): can you paste the curl or the request id? which model and sdk/version?
Tony (Customer): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query":"long query...","documents":[...150 docs...]}'
Tony (Customer): each doc ~1-2k chars, query ~900 chars. if we trim to 50 docs it's fine.
Maya (Support): sounds like you're hitting the rerank payload ceiling. current proxy + service cap is ~1MB. we should surface a clearer error. filing asap.
Lee (Eng): quick add: 413 can come from nginx proxy (client_max_body_size) OR our input validator which enforces max_payload_bytes=1048576. Tokens/bytes computed after UTF-8 and tokenizer; long unicode can bloat size.
Tony (Customer): ugh. will this be considered a bug or expected limit? customers confused by 'Payload too large'.
Maya (Support): UX note: the message is opaque. I'm opening a support KB entry and escalating to eng to return a clearer error like 'input size exceeds rerank limit: X bytes' and include request_id.
Lee (Eng): workaround: pre-filter candidates via embeddings (cheap) or send in chunks: do binary search over doc count to find cut-off and then rerank top candidates. also consider truncating passages or sending only passages/IDs for rerank.
Sam (Billing): FYI failed 413s are not billed for token usage; we only bill successful rerank responses. I'll add a KB note so CS can reassure customers.
deploy-bot: [system] 2179991302 rerank-service reject id=abc123 size=1223345 bytes
Maya (Support): Tony — if you can share request id abc123 and timeframe we'll pull logs. I'll follow up with PR #4521 when error text change is in.
Tony (Customer): thanks all — will share logs if it happens again. in the meantime we switched to pre-filter + smaller batches and it's OK :+1:
Maya (Support): great, closing interim ticket but keeping eng follow-up. thanks :slightly_smiling_face:
